abstract: BACKGROUND: The association of urogenital (UG) anomalies and sacrococcygeal teratoma (SCT) has not been widely reported. Our aim was to look at the national incidence and presentation of this anomaly in patients with SCT and to provide the first report of a clear anatomical description of this commonly missed association. METHODS: Sacrococcygeal teratoma cases in Scotland during the last 30 years were identified. Patients with associated UG anomalies were reviewed in detail to identify their presentation, anatomy, and management. RESULTS: Fifty-three patients with SCT were identified, including 41 girls. Five girls (12%) subsequently had a UG anomaly diagnosed, which was not apparent at the initial surgery. Two patients presented with retention, and their anomaly was diagnosed at 6 weeks and 7 months of age. The other 3 presented with incontinence, and despite thorough assessment, including cystoscopy, their UG anomalies were not recognized until the ages of 7, 9, and 13 years. CONCLUSIONS: Urogenital anomalies are surprisingly common in girls with SCT. The reason for this association is unclear. None of these cases were diagnosed initially, which means that it was either missed or acquired. Urogenital anomalies should be suspected in girls with SCT and actively excluded in those with voiding difficulties.
abstract_ja: 背景：尿生殖器（UG）奇形と仙尾部奇形腫（SCT）の関連は、これまで広く報告されていない。本研究の目的は、SCTを有する患者におけるこの奇形の全国的な発生率と臨床像を調べ、この見過ごされやすい関連について明確な解剖学的記述を初めて報告することである。方法：スコットランドにおける過去30年間のSCT症例を同定した。関連するUG奇形を有する患者を詳細にレビューし、その臨床像、解剖学、および管理を特定した。結果：SCT患者53例（女児41例を含む）が同定された。女児5例（12%）で、初回手術時には明らかでなかったUG奇形が後に診断された。2例は排尿困難（尿閉）で受診し、生後6週と7か月で奇形が診断された。他の3例は失禁で受診し、膀胱鏡検査を含む詳細な評価を行ったにもかかわらず、7歳、9歳、13歳までUG奇形は認識されなかった。結論：SCTの女児にはUG奇形が驚くほど多い。この関連の理由は不明である。これらの症例はいずれも初回診断されなかったため、見逃されたか、後天的に生じたかのいずれかである。SCTの女児ではUG奇形を疑い、排尿障害のある児では積極的に除外すべきである。
